title: Protocol for Biofilm Streamer Formation in a Microfluidic Device with Micro-pillars
protocol: Design the mask with appropriate software.
Print this design on glass coated with approximately 70 nm thick layer of Chromium (Cr), using masking in order to prepare a photo mask.
Use AZ400K developer for 1 min.
Etch the Cr layer using Cr etchant for about 1 min.
Strip the resist with acetone and clean it with cold piranha solution.
Clean a standard 4" silicon wafer chemically with piranha solution for 20 min.
Rinse the wafer with DI water and dry it.
Heat the wafer on a hot plate (200 °C for 15 min).
Coat the silicon wafer with photoresist AZ4620.
Spin-coat the wafer at 2,000 rpm for 25 seconds to achieve a 12.5 μm thick layer.
Soft bake the wafer on a hot plate at 100 °C by floating it on nitrogen flow for 90 seconds.
Vacuum bake the wafer at 100 °C for 60 seconds.
Place the wafer in a dark box for dehydration for 24 hours.
Expose the wafer to UV light to transfer the designed pattern to the photoresist.
Immerse the wafer in AZ400K developer solution for 240 seconds.
Rinse the wafer with isopropyl alcohol.
Dry the wafer using a stream of nitrogen gas.
Apply DRIE etching with an appropriate etch depth (50 μm).
Remove remaining photoresist with acetone.
Clean the wafer after removing the photoresist.
Use trichloromethylsilane (TCMS) for silanizing the silicon master mold.
Place 2-3 drops of TCMS in a vial and position it beside the silicon master mold in a desiccator.
Allow the silanizing process to complete over 2-3 hours.
Mix Sylgard 184 silicone base with curing agent by weight ratio of 10:1 to prepare PDMS.
Degas the PDMS under vacuum conditions for about 2 hours.
Put the silicon master mold in a holder.
Pour PDMS on the silicon master mold to form the stamp.
Cure the PDMS for 2 hours at 80 °C.
Peel off the PDMS stamp from the master mold.
Cut the PDMS stamp into separate microchips.
Use a cutting core to drill holes for the inlet(s) and outlet(s).
Expose the cover slip and PDMS stamp to oxygen plasma for 30 seconds.
Bond PDMS stamp to the cover slip.
Anneal the device by putting it in an oven at 70 °C for 10 minutes.
Add 20 g of Luria-Bertani (LB) agar powders and 500 ml of ultrapure water to a 1 L flask.
Stir to dissolve the powder.
Sterilize the mixture by autoclaving at 15 psi, 121 °C for 15 minutes.
Allow the flask to cool down to 50-55 °C on a bench or in a water bath.
Add Tetracycline antibiotic to achieve a final concentration of 50 μg/ml.
Mix well by swirling.
Pour the mixture into plates until each plate is 1/2 - 2/3 full.
Flame air bubbles briefly if they form.
Allow the plates to cool at room temperature overnight.
Add 20 g Luria-Bertani (LB) broth powders and 1 L of ultrapure water to a flask.
Stir the mixture until the powder is dissolved.
Sterilize by autoclaving at 15 psi, 121 °C for 15 min.
Allow the flask to cool down to 50-55°C on a bench or in a water bath.
Add tetracycline to achieve a final concentration of 50 μg/ml and mix well by swirling.
Cover the bottle with tin foil and store at 4 °C.
Take the bacterial stock from the freezer (-80 °C) and place it on ice.
Place the -80 °C bacterial stock and an LB agar plate inside a biosafety hood.
Streak the bacterial strain onto an LB agar plate in a zigzag pattern.
Cover the agar plate and incubate at 30 ºC overnight.
Store the plate in the refrigerator at 4 °C.
Pour 50 ml LB broth media to an autoclaved flask inside a biosafety hood.
Transfer a single bacterial colony from the LB agar plate to the flask, inside a biosafety hood.
Put the flask in a shaker incubator at 30 °C and 150 rpm for adequate time (4 hr).
Pour 5 ml LB broth media into a sterilized plastic tube.
Dilute S1 by mixing with LB broth media.
Vortex the solution.
Measure the optical density of the solution at 600 nm to achieve an OD = 0.1.
Using tweezers, connect flexible plastic tubes (0.20" ID) into the inlet(s) and outlet(s) of the microchip.
Fill syringe(s) with bacterial solution (S2 solution).
Remove all bubbles from the syringe(s).
Connect syringe tip(s) to inlet tube(s) using 30 G 0.5" blunt needle.
Connect outlet tube(s) to a waste container.
Place and fix syringe(s) onto the syringe pump.
Place the microchip under an optical microscope with objective lenses of desired magnification (e.g., 40X).
Cover the microchip with a live cell chamber device to maintain a constant temperature environment for bacterial growth (30 °C for P. fluorescens).
Set the pump to the desired flow rate level (say 10 μl/hr).
Initiate fluid pumping.
Introduce bacteria into the chamber for biofilm formation.
Observe and take images of biofilm growth through the microscope.
